acceptance: A manually invoked release command for a tagged source revision produces immutable artifacts and evidence without manual source edits, binding vector-dispatch source commit, tree, CRYPT_VECTOR_DISPATCH_V2, and release generation.
verifiedBy: node --test scripts/release/pipeline/pipeline.test.mjs (17/17 pass, executed -- see commands.log). node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-903 (the manifest command) was not run; per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md the manifest commands list runs once at the final phased book gate, not per task.
observed: scripts/release/pipeline/multi-platform-release.mjs's CLI (`node scripts/release/pipeline/multi-platform-release.mjs --tag vX.Y.Z --version X.Y.Z [--commit SHA --tree SHA] [--write]`) is the manually invoked release command for a tagged source revision. It resolves commit/tree read-only from git (or accepts them explicitly), computes one deterministic release_generation binding product+CRYPT_VECTOR_DISPATCH_V2+commit+tree+version+the ordered four-target set (identity.mjs's computeReleaseGeneration, tested for byte-identical determinism across repeated calls and for changing only when an input changes), reads whatever RightKit has already sealed per platform without re-implementing MBR-901/MBR-902's own verification (sealed-platforms.mjs reusing scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs and scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs), and writes one immutable evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json binding all four targets' status to that single commit. Immutability is enforced, not asserted: writeImmutableReleaseGeneration is idempotent for an unchanged plan and throws ImmutableReleaseConflictError rather than overwriting a changed one under the same releaseId (tested). Drift across the two machines in Adrian's real workflow -- Mac sealed at commit A, Windows sealed manifest naming commit B under what looks like the same release path -- throws ReleaseDriftError and is never silently merged into one release (tested, three cases: single-target read, whole-plan build, and the immutable-write layer). No manual source edit is required or performed: every input is either resolved from git read-only or passed explicitly; nothing here edits application source.
gap: This task ships the orchestration layer and its deterministic tests; it does not itself produce a real signed macOS/Windows release. That still requires: (1) running `pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub release:doctor` then `release:build:mac` on a macOS machine holding the Developer ID/notarization credentials (MBR-901's job), and `release:build:win` on a Windows machine holding Azure Artifact Signing credentials (MBR-902's job) -- both explicitly forbidden from this task by its hard rules (never run cargo/pnpm/Tauri/right-release/signing commands here); and (2) then running this task's own `multi-platform-release.mjs --write` on each of those two machines to bind their real sealed output into one evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json. CONFIRMED, NOT NEW, GAP (inherited from apps/membrane-hub's packaging config, outside this task's and MBR-901/902's allowed scope): apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs's targets.mac packages only an aarch64 DMG and targets.win only an x64 NSIS installer, so mac-x64 and windows-arm64 have no RightKit build to read; platform-targets.mjs records this honestly as not-buildable/conformance-only rather than fabricating a verified status, and docs/release/pipeline.md documents it. This is deferred to the Book 3 final phased gate, consistent with MBR-901's and MBR-902's own acceptance.json gap notes.
